src/user/user.controller.ts: UserController.login() builds the auth result `{email, token, username, bio, image}` itself rather than getting a finished result from the service
src/user/user.controller.ts: findMe, update, create and delete each pass the whole operation to one UserService call, which is correct for presentation
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of `UserController` does what a presentation layer should. It maps routes, binds parameters, runs validation pipes, adds Swagger annotations and passes work to `UserService`. The `login` handler is the exception. It runs the login flow inside the controller: it looks up the user with the supplied credentials, decides that a missing user means login fails, then calls `generateJWT` and builds the user response object with the token. Doing these steps in this order is the authentication use case, which belongs in the application layer (`UserService`). The other handlers each pass the whole operation to one service call. Turning the failure into an HTTP 401 and shaping the response are fine in presentation. Running the steps in sequence and deciding when to issue a token is not. This is borderline because the logic is small and close to request handling.

violations.message: UserController.login() runs the login use case itself: it looks up the user by credentials, treats a missing user as a login failure, calls generateJWT, and builds the authenticated user object with the token. This orchestration belongs in the application layer (UserService, e.g. a single login method). The controller should only call that method and turn its result or error into HTTP.
